 The NBA landscape shifted over a wild summer. Here’s a look at every team’s new starting lineup, ranked from bottom to top. Blake Silverman | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source The 76ers loaded up over the offseason, but will it work? | Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE/Getty Images In this story:

--> A long summer of monumental player movement across the NBA reshaped the league’s landscape.
 Teams took note of where they succeeded and, well, failed last season. With that, swift roster changes were made. Some teams tweaked their personnel and others fully upended last year’s group. Milwaukee no longer has a superstar , which makes Miami richer . Philadelphia brought in one star, which led to the greatest scorer of all time taking his talents—or, maybe, his helicopter—to town as well. 
--> Teams took note of where they succeeded and, well, failed last season. With that, swift roster changes were made. Some teams tweaked their personnel and others fully upended last year’s group. Milwaukee no longer has a superstar , which makes Miami richer . Philadelphia brought in one star, which led to the greatest scorer of all time taking his talents—or, maybe, his helicopter—to town as well. 
 Others were more casual with their offseason approach and didn’t rock the boat or give up a ton of assets and future flexibility for short-term possibilities. We’ll find out what strategy and subsequent team worked best once the new NBA season begins on Tuesday. In the meantime, we wanted to take a look at each team around the league to see how the shuffled lineups stack up against the competition. Benches are important, but the first five is the group that sets the tone and, more often than not, finishes games.

 30. Los Angeles Clippers 
--> 30. Los Angeles Clippers 
 Projected starters: Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Brook Lopez, Keaton Wagler
 --> Projected starters: Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Brook Lopez, Keaton Wagler
 I’m sorry to kick you while you’re down, Clippers fans. If Brandon Ingram was healthy, I promise your starting lineup wouldn’t fall last. It’s unclear how much time Ingram will miss to start the year, but his absence provides more immediate offensive opportunities for Keaton Wagler, the No. 5 pick in the draft. After the league brought the hammer down on the Clippers over the summer following the Kawhi Leonard cap circumvention saga, Wagler’s development has to be the most important thing for the franchise moving forward. Darius Garland should have a good year and Rui Hachimura will help, but Tyronn Lue’s top priority should be getting Wagler opportunities.

 29. Milwaukee Bucks 
--> 29. Milwaukee Bucks 
 Projected starters: Tyler Herro, Myles Turner, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Ryan Rollins, Kyle Kuzma
 --> Projected starters: Tyler Herro, Myles Turner, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Ryan Rollins, Kyle Kuzma
 Milwaukee enters a new era without Giannis Antetokounmpo. The franchise chose Miami’s future-forward package of young players and draft capital over Boston’s centered around Jaylen Brown. Brown would’ve helped the team stay afloat immediately, but the Bucks made the right move. Unfortunately, that means it will be tough sledding right out of the gate. Tyler Herro brings some juice as he plays for his hometown team and Ryan Rollins could take another leap, but Milwaukee simply doesn’t have the star power anymore.

 I’m sorry Grizzlies fans, I really am excited about your team. Until we see Cameron Boozer actually dominate at the next level alongside a healthy Zach Edey, though, this Memphis group resides near the bottom compared to other first fives. Over the offseason, the franchise finally parted with Ja Morant after Jaren Jackson Jr. and Desmond Bane were dealt within the past year. It’s a new era for the Grizzlies and the organization should be excited with a future All-Star in Boozer.

 27. Brooklyn Nets 
--> 27. Brooklyn Nets 
 Michael Porter Jr. gets more scoring in Brooklyn this year with Julius Randle’s arrival | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Projected starters: Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, Day’Ron Sharpe, Egor Dëmin, Mikel Brown Jr.
 --> Projected starters: Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, Day’Ron Sharpe, Egor Dëmin, Mikel Brown Jr.
 The Nets should be better this season after they took Julius Randle’s contract from Minnesota. However, will the presence of Randle and Michael Porter Jr. impact the development of the franchise’s young core ? Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Dëmin’s growth should be priority No. 1. As a rookie, Brown needs to show flashes and prove that Brooklyn made the right decision taking him over other guards they passed on like Darius Acuff Jr., Kingston Flemings and Brayden Burries. As currently constructed, though, the Nets’ lineup can’t compete with the top teams in the Eastern Conference, no matter how nice their new ABA-inspired jerseys look.

 26. Sacramento Kings

Maybe this is the year Sacramento moves off one or both of them as the franchise pivots fully into its Darius Acuff Jr. era. The flashy guard’s development is key for the Kings, and you have to hope the surrounding team raises his floor.

 25. New Orleans Pelicans 
--> 25. New Orleans Pelicans 
 Projected starters: Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III, Herbert Jones, Dejounte Murray, Yves Missi
 --> Projected starters: Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III, Herbert Jones, Dejounte Murray, Yves Missi
 It’s a shame that Jeremiah Fears nor Derik Queen are likely to start for New Orleans considering they are two building blocks. New coach Jamahl Mosley will likely experiment with his rotations and opportunities will open up throughout the year. As of now, though, the Pelicans have an odd roster. We’ll see what’s in store for Zion Williamson after this year (or at the trade deadline), but him and Dejounte Murray plus Fears, Queen, Jordan Poole and Bennedict Mathurin off the bench limits offensive chances for each player due to the sheer volume of guys who need shots. The Pels may be better than last year, but the front office needs to choose a direction.

 24. Charlotte Hornets 
--> 24. Charlotte Hornets 
 Projected starters: Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel, Coby White, Naz Reid, Moussa Diabaté
 --> Projected starters: Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel, Coby White, Naz Reid, Moussa Diabaté
 The Hornets went a completely different direction over the offseason by trading LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges. Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel now have the keys to the franchise, while Miller specifically needs to prove he’s capable of being the No. 1 option on a playoff team. This year might be too soon, but it’s a critical year for Miller, who’s yet to come to terms with Charlotte on a rookie extension. Coby White remains to conduct the offense, while Naz Reid was a huge addition through the Ball trade. While the Hornets may seem weak at center, that was the concern last year and Moussa Diabaté was an impactful starting big man.

 23. Chicago Bulls 
--> 23. Chicago Bulls 
 No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson has brought a ton of excitement to Chicago | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Projected starters: Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson, Norman Powell, Nic Claxton
 --> Projected starters: Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, Caleb Wilson, Norman Powell, Nic Claxton
 We’re all excited about No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson , but the Bulls have a pretty solid starting five outside of the prized rookie forward. Chicago could be frisky this year, likely not good enough to truly compete, but Norman Powell and Nic Claxton were strong additions over the offseason to raise the floor of the young team. Matas Buzelis could take a leap and Josh Giddey was putting up All-Star numbers before an untimely injury last year. I like what the Bulls are building.

 21. Dallas Mavericks 
--> 21. Dallas Mavericks 
 Kyrie Irving will make his return to the court this season | REUTERS Projected starters: Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, P.J. Washington, Daniel Gafford
 --> Projected starters: Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, P.J. Washington, Daniel Gafford
 Kyrie Irving’s return is exciting and, even if the Mavericks probably should trade him, Dallas wants to see how he helps Cooper Flagg’s continued growth into NBA superstardom. Outside of Irving and Flagg, the roster is fairly jumbled. Maybe Santi Aldama or Dereck Lively II starts instead of Daniel Gafford. Maybe No. 9 pick Morez Johnson Jr. should play next to Flagg more often than not. If new coach Dusty May can make it all work, Flagg could take the Mavs back to the playoffs sooner than anticipated. He’s that good.

 20. Los Angeles Lakers 
--> 20. Los Angeles Lakers 
 Projected starters: Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia
 --> Projected starters: Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia
 The Lakers are fully Luka Dončić’s team with LeBron James’s departure over the offseason. The new-look roster is fully catered to Dončić’s needs and locking down Austin Reaves over the offseason was key. Walker Kessler joins the core group as Luka’s big man and lob threat after his arrival through a sign-and-trade with Utah. With Dončić and Reaves, though, there are some serious questions on the defensive end.

 19. Phoenix Suns 
--> 19. Phoenix Suns 
 Projected starters: Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks, Jalen Green, Miles Bridges, Oso Ighodaro
 --> Projected starters: Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks, Jalen Green, Miles Bridges, Oso Ighodaro
 Mark Williams’s injury stings, which leaves a concern for Phoenix at center. Maybe it’s Oso Ighodaro, maybe Khaman Maluach is ready to step in. Outside of that, the Suns have a solid first unit. Bridges was the big acquisition , an upgrade that came at the price of depth in Grayson Allen and Royce O’Neale. Dillon Brooks had a career season last year that earned him a solid extension as one of Devin Booker’s running mates. Jalen Green was up-and-down, but he had some big moments to get the Suns into the playoffs through the play-in tournament. The franchise could move on from him, mainly due to his big $36 million player option for 2027-28. In the meantime, though, he’s a scoring threat that takes pressure off of Booker.

 The Magic were on the verge of a massive upset, but Orlando blew a 3–1 lead on the top-seeded Pistons in the first round of the playoffs. They made no significant changes over the summer other than the hiring of Sean Sweeney as the franchise’s new coach. He should do wonders as a top assistant who was bound for a solid head coaching job. The Magic need to take the next step after a first-round exit in three straight seasons. If Franz Wagner is healthy, anything is possible. But it will be tough sledding in the loaded East.
